records.description: DCENT disclosed abnormal unauthorized asset transfers involving its software App Wallet while separately stating that no impact originating from the hardware wallets themselves had been confirmed. Independent XRPL on-chain analysis traced an initial September 15 sweep of 1,552 wallets and later reported at least 6,633 wallets and 10,137,230 XRP across additional waves through September 20.
records.notes: Root cause remains unresolved in DCENT's public incident reporting. DCENT's September 17 action-scope notice narrows the confirmed exposure boundary to App Wallet use in app versions earlier than 8.1.0 where the user signed transactions; v8.1.0 was released on 2025-11-05. This scope statement is not treated as a public root-cause disclosure or proof that 8.1.0 was a remediation release. DCENT's guidance also applies when a hardware-wallet recovery phrase was ever imported into App Wallet, because that phrase then entered the software-wallet trust boundary. XRPL.to's current featured on-chain summary reports six waves through 2026-09-20 totaling 6,633 wallets and 10,137,230 XRP, with 5,001 emptied XRPL accounts later deleted for reserves and 5.6 million XRP swapped to Ethereum through THORChain. The newer 6,678-wallet / 11.7M-XRP figures visible in the operator-provided social screenshot remain a discovery signal pending a directly retrievable supporting source.
records.title: Mass unauthorized transfers affected DCENT App Wallet users
